findings.title: Temporary secret buffers are not consistently cleared on exceptional exits
findings.status: confirmed; existing defense-in-depth gap; all reviewed baselines
findings.condition: generateKeySet creates the spending scalar before creating the viewing scalar; a subsequent RNG or public-key operation can throw before ownership is returned. In the bearer-encrypted invoice path, the generated AES key is cleared only after successful encryption, and the decrypt path does not clear its temporary decoded key or plaintext byte array.
findings.impact: These temporary byte arrays remain eligible for garbage collection rather than being explicitly overwritten. This is a best-effort memory-hygiene gap. No remote read primitive, disclosure, signature bypass, or fund-loss path was established. JavaScript strings and runtime copies cannot be guaranteed to be erased.
findings.remediation: Use an exception-safe scope/try-finally for newly created secret buffers. Transfer ownership only on successful key-set construction. Retain and clear the temporary AES key and plaintext arrays after use, while documenting unavoidable string/runtime copies.
findings.validation_criterion: With a controlled failing dependency, already-created temporary buffers are cleared on each failure path; successful key generation retains the returned secrets. Assess through ordinary isolated unit assertions, without live targets or crafted attack files.
findings.notes: The core key-generation part was already recorded as I-02. SecretScope and SecretBox provide working cleanup patterns, and their source tests were read. This finding does not imply SecretBox itself exposes its stored bytes.

findings.title: QR image pixel bounds can be checked only after native allocation for unsupported headers
findings.condition: The file picker accepts raster image MIME types beyond the PNG/GIF/JPEG/WebP headers inspected by imageHeaderDimensions. For an unrecognized header, decodeQrImage calls createImageBitmap before checking the universal pixel cap.
findings.impact: A user-selected image in a platform-supported format whose header is not inspected may consume native decoder resources before the 40-million-pixel limit rejects it. The input still has a 10 MiB compressed-file cap and decoded resources are closed. Actual browser memory behavior was not measured; this is a local availability limitation, not a demonstrated remote exploit.
findings.remediation: Restrict imports to formats with a reliable pre-decode dimension check, extend supported header inspection, or use an appropriately resource-bounded image decoding path. Keep the post-decode check as a second control.
findings.validation_criterion: Every accepted file format is rejected or dimension-checked before the native decoder allocates its full bitmap. Existing small stubbed decoder assertions can verify ordering; no oversized image need be generated or opened.
findings.notes: The existing test explicitly documents post-decode fallback for HEIC/AVIF. No image was generated, opened, or used to reproduce resource exhaustion.

findings.title: Rejected conflicting QR chunks refresh the idle deadline on older baselines
findings.status: confirmed on main/release; corrected on completion and qr-idle-fix
findings.condition: On main and release, Assembler updates lastActivity before rejecting a conflicting chunk. Latest completion moves that update after validation.
findings.impact: Rejected input can prolong a bounded partial QR session beyond the intended idle deadline. This does not bypass final payload integrity or authentication and does not create unbounded storage.
findings.remediation: Retain the latest ordering, where only accepted activity refreshes the deadline.
findings.validation_criterion: A rejected conflict preserves the previous deadline; the next operation after that deadline reports session expiry. Accepted duplicates retain their explicitly intended refresh behavior.

findings.title: Canonical arrays were not restricted to dense own data properties on main
findings.status: confirmed API hardening gap on main/base64-fix; corrected on release/completion/qr-idle-fix
findings.condition: The main canonicalizer calls an input array map method and does not reject sparse/decorated arrays or snapshot data descriptors. Latest versions validate and snapshot dense own data properties before recursion.
findings.impact: Malformed JavaScript API inputs can have unexpected or ambiguous canonical representations. A reachable signature bypass through the strict JSON invoice parser was not established; parsed JSON supplies ordinary dense arrays.
findings.remediation: Retain the descriptor-based latest implementation and its regression tests.
findings.validation_criterion: Malformed sparse/decorated/accessor arrays fail closed; supported dense arrays retain identical canonical bytes and array membership/value traps are not invoked.

findings.title: Base64url decoder lacks an explicit runtime string guard on main
findings.status: confirmed API hardening gap on main; corrected on release/completion and both fix heads
findings.condition: The main exported decoder reads text.length and charCodeAt without checking that the runtime argument is a string. All later reviewed versions add the explicit type guard.
findings.impact: Malformed direct JavaScript caller inputs can be accepted as empty data or produce inconsistent errors. The invoice fragment entry point already checks its string input, so no remote invoice-verification bypass was established.
findings.remediation: Retain the latest explicit string guard and fixed decoder error.
findings.validation_criterion: All non-string direct API inputs receive the same typed decoder failure before allocation or iteration.

findings.title: Merchant profile expiry accepts an invalid caller clock on older baselines
findings.status: confirmed on main/base64-fix; corrected on release/completion/qr-idle-fix
findings.condition: The older verifier compares exp with the supplied nowSec without first rejecting invalid clocks. Latest versions reject non-finite and negative clocks.
findings.impact: A caller supplying an invalid clock can receive a valid result for an otherwise correctly signed profile whose expiry cannot be meaningfully evaluated. Control of the clock is a caller/environment prerequisite; no external clock-control path was established.
findings.validation_criterion: Invalid clocks fail with a format result; correct clocks preserve the exclusive expiry boundary.

scope_observations.title: SDK merchant response size limit follows full body materialization
scope_observations.status: confirmed implementation limitation; outside active Pages runtime
scope_observations.severity: Low if SDK merchant transport is in deployment scope; otherwise informational
scope_observations.detail: merchant.ts awaits res.text() before enforcing MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS, and has only an optional caller-provided abort signal. A configured service or faulty endpoint can consume response-body memory/time before rejection. No SDK import was found in apps/web/src or apps/web/public at completion. No service was contacted.
scope_observations.remediation: Before enabling this SDK transport, use a bounded streaming read and an explicit timeout/abort policy. An injected transport should expose equivalent resource limits.
scope_observations.validation_criterion: The client aborts reading at its configured byte budget and deadline without materializing an unbounded body.

scope_observations.title: SDK invoice-status responses are not bound to the requested nonce
scope_observations.status: confirmed API consistency gap; outside active Pages runtime
scope_observations.severity: Informational; assess deployment-specific reliance before promotion
scope_observations.detail: getInvoiceStatus and registerInvoice parse the returned nonce shape but do not compare it to the requested invoice nonce. A faulty or misrouted API response can be returned for the wrong invoice. A malicious API already controls the reported payment status; independent payment authenticity is not established by this SDK transport.
scope_observations.remediation: Require returned nonce equality for status/register responses and make callers retain their independently selected invoice identity.
scope_observations.validation_criterion: A well-formed response for a different nonce is rejected as a response mismatch.

scope_observations.title: Permit domain name/version are outside the tx-review intent comparison
scope_observations.status: retired as active Pages vulnerability after caller inspection
scope_observations.detail: decodeTypedData requires nonempty permit name/version but omits them from PermitSigIntent. The current Pages permit path separately builds and checks the domain through buildPermit and the on-chain DOMAIN_SEPARATOR comparison before signing. No active ungated caller was established. Consumers using tx-review alone should retain this separate domain check.
scope_observations.remediation: Document the required domain check for standalone consumers, or include a trusted expected domain in the review contract if the library is intended to provide that guarantee.
scope_observations.validation_criterion: Any supported signing path validates the complete permit domain before requesting a signature.

delegated_candidates.title: Receipt issuedAt permits safe integers outside a displayable Date range
delegated_candidates.status: candidate delegated to parent/payment reviewer; not a confirmed impact here
delegated_candidates.detail: validateReceiptPayload only requires a positive safe integer for issuedAt. Inspect actual receipt rendering/export consumers for safe handling before assigning severity. This is not a receipt signature bypass. Parent acknowledged routing it to the payment reviewer.

retired_hypotheses: A minimal signed receipt may intentionally omit the stealth address. The signature still binds its present fields and receipt verification is explicitly distinct from independent payment evidence; this is not a forged-payment finding.
Bearer-encrypted invoice links intentionally carry the encryption key in the fragment. Link-holder readability is the documented model, not a cryptographic break.
A valid self-signature is intentionally distinct from a pinned seller identity. Latest and main strict-pin behavior was reviewed; no pin bypass was established.
QR checksums and short session identifiers provide transport integrity, not peer authentication. Configuration imports require caller review and signed invoice payloads retain their own verification.

SecretScalar is a redaction guardrail with documented JavaScript copy limitations; SecretBox stores bytes separately and lends wiped copies. Guardrail limits were not promoted to arbitrary secret disclosure.
Non-EVM structural address/URI helpers and SDK merchant operations do not establish active Pages payment exposure. Their code was read, but no deployment or live service was assessed.
